data.name: Sadashiva
data.gender_notes: Sadashiva is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sadashiva is a form of Lord Shiva, representing the eternal, unchanging aspect of the god. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'sada' (eternal) and 'shiva' (god). The name Sadashiva carries the meaning “The eternal lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Sadashiva usually hope their child will grow to embody the eternal lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sadashiva signifies the eternal, unchanging nature of the divine and represents the ultimate reality and the highest consciousness. It is a reminder of the eternal nature of the soul and the universe.
data.etymology: Sadashiva belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “The eternal lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadashiva total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Sadashiva is a revered deity in Hinduism, particularly in the Shaivite tradition, where devotion to Lord Shiva is paramount. Sadashiva is often depicted in art and iconography, particularly in temple sculptures and paintings. He is a symbol of stability, strength, and the eternal nature of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: Sadashiva represents the ultimate reality and the source of all creation. He is the embodiment of pure consciousness and the destroyer of ignorance. Devotion to Sadashiva is believed to bring spiritual growth, purification of the mind, and a deeper understanding of the ultimate truth. In meditation, invoking the name "Sadashiva" helps in focusing the mind on the eternal and unchanging reality of the self and the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sadashiva signifies the eternal and unchanging aspect of Lord Shiva, representing the absolute truth and consciousness beyond all illusion and change. It is a reminder of the divine presence that transcends the limitations of time and form.

historical_references.reference: Sadashiva is a form of Shiva in Hinduism, representing absolute consciousness and supreme being. He is often depicted as a three-eyed god, with a third eye symbolizing wisdom and inner vision. This form of Shiva is known to have originated during the Late Vedic Period (around 500 BCE).

Sadashiva is also associated with the Shaiva and Shakti traditions of Hinduism. In these traditions, Sadashiva is considered to be the supreme deity, beyond even Shiva and Shakti. He is often depicted with his consort, Prakriti or Parvati, symbolizing the union of consciousness and matter. This form of Sadashiva became popular during the medieval period (600-1300 CE).

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, the name 'Sadashiva' is popularly used in spiritual, meditation, and yoga communities. Sadashiva is considered the supreme deity of the Hindu trimurti, representing the eternal, unchanging aspect of Shiva. On Instagram, Sadashiva is often depicted in art and imagery, with hashtags like #Sadashiva and #Shiva used to discover related content. On Reddit, there are several communities dedicated to Sadashiva, where users discuss his significance, mythology, and symbolism. On Quora, there are questions related to 'Who is Sadashiva?' and 'What are the powers of Sadashiva?', reflecting the enduring curiosity about this deity.
